extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users and developers (mathematicians, numerical programmers, and system administrators compiling/configuring PARI/GP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP command semantics, parallel primitives, and the gp 'defaults' configuration options; also contains build/configure and installation guidance for Unix. Useful for users tuning behavior, enabling parallelism, or compiling PARI/GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: parforvec / parfor behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: parforvec(X = v, expr1, {j}, {expr2}, {flag}) evaluates expr2 (dependent on X and j) for X as generated by forvec, in random order, computed in parallel. Substitute for j the value of expr1 (dependent on X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations are done in random order and in parallel. It is allowed for expr2 to exit the loop using break/next/return; however in that case expr2 will still be evaluated for all remaining values of p less than the current one, unless a subsequent break/next/return happens.

rubrics_metrics.name: parselect
rubrics_metrics.description: parselect(f, A, {flag = 0}) selects elements of A according to the selection function f, done in parallel. If flag is 1, return the indices of those elements (indirect selection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function f must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Library syntax: GEN parselect(GEN f, GEN A, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: parsum
rubrics_metrics.description: parsum(i = a, b, expr, {x}) computes the sum of expression expr (initialized at x) with the formal parameter i running from a to b, evaluated in parallel in random order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression expr must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Example: parsum(i=1,1000,ispseudoprime(2^prime(i)-1)) returns the number of prime numbers among the first 1000 Mersenne numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: parvector
rubrics_metrics.description: parvector(N, i, expr) is like vector(N,i,expr) but the evaluations of expr are done in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression expr must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Example: parvector(10,i,quadclassunit(2^(100+i)+1).no) computes class numbers in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeXstyle default bits
rubrics_metrics.description: TeXstyle: bits that allow gp to use less rigid TeX formatting commands in the logfile (only considered when log = 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bit meanings: 2 = insert \right/\left where appropriate; 4 = insert discretionary breaks in polynomials to enhance line breaking. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: breakloop default
rubrics_metrics.description: breakloop: enables the 'break loop' debugging mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is 1 if running interactive gp session, otherwise 0. See Section 2.10.3 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: colors default and format
rubrics_metrics.description: colors: a string or token selecting colors used by gp output (only usable in color-capable terminals). Accepted values are strings "a1,...,ak" where k <= 7 and each ai is 'no', an integer 0..15, or a triple [c0,c1,c2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven output objects affected are error messages, history numbers, prompt, input line, output, help messages, timer. If k<7, remaining are assumed 'no'. Special values darkbg/lightbg/boldfg map to preset palettes. Incompatible with PariEmacs (change fails silently). Default is "" (no colors). Example: default(colors, "9, 5, no, no, 4"). See misc/color.dft for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: compatible (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: compatible: obsolete default, now a no-op.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented as obsolete; no behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: datadir default
rubrics_metrics.description: datadir: name of directory containing optional data files (elldata, galdata, galpol, seadata packages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is /usr/local/share/pari or override specified via Configure --datadir=.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug default
rubrics_metrics.description: debug: debugging level; non-zero prints extra messages according to context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0. See \g for related commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: debugfiles default
rubrics_metrics.description: debugfiles: file usage debugging level; non-zero prints information on file descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0. See \gf.

rubrics_metrics.name: debugmem default and note
rubrics_metrics.description: debugmem: memory debugging level; non-zero causes regular printing of memory usage info and when >2 indicates garbage collection and function involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is 0. Important note: memory usage printing is disabled unless running a version compiled for debugging (see Appendix A), because it noticeably slows performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: echo toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: echo: 1 or 0. When on, each command is reprinted before execution (useful for reading files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 0. It is turned on in test files used to check gp. See \e.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor add primes
rubrics_metrics.description: factor_add_primes: if on (1), integer factorization machinery calls addprimes on prime factors that were difficult to find, so they are tried first in other factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps recover prime factors found before an interruption; downside: a huge addprimes table unrelated to current computations slows arithmetic functions relying on factorization. Use removeprimes to empty the table. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor_proven toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: factor_proven: if on (1), factors output by integer factorization machinery are proven primes; otherwise they are pseudoprimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When set, primality proof is done for each factor and results depending on factorization are fully proven. Does not affect explicitly requested partial factorization nor private addprimes table entries. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: format default (x.n)
rubrics_metrics.description: format: of the form x.n where x in {e,f,g} controls conversion style and n is precision (integer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: e = scientific format with explicit exponent; f = fixed floating format (large reals with ill-defined integer part printed in e); g = f except when decimal exponent < -4 then e; n is number of significant digits printed unless n<0 prints all digits. Default is "g.28" on 32-bit, "g.38" on 64-bit. For more formatting use printf/Strprintf.

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolormap
rubrics_metrics.description: graphcolormap: vector of colors for hi-res graphing routines; must contain at least 3 entries (background, frame/ticks, axes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colors may be strings (lowercase, no whitespace) or RGB codes [r,g,b] with integers 0..255. All colormap entries can be used in plotcolor calls. Default is ["white","black","blue","violetred","red","green","grey","gainsboro"]. See rgb.txt for valid names.

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolors
rubrics_metrics.description: graphcolors: indices into graphcolormap used to plot multi-curves; successive curves cycle through this list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is [4,5]. Curves drawn in graphcolormap[graphcolors[1]], graphcolormap[graphcolors[2]], etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: help default
rubrics_metrics.description: help: name of external help program used from within gp when extended help is invoked (??, ??? or M-H under readline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is the path to the gphelp script installed with PARI.

rubrics_metrics.name: histfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: histfile: name of file where gp keeps history of input commands (results omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file exists when histfile changes, it is read and becomes part of session history. Setting in gprc saves readline history between sessions. Empty string sets histfile to <undefined>. Default is <undefined>.

rubrics_metrics.name: histsize
rubrics_metrics.description: histsize: number of last results gp keeps in history (recoverable via % notation). Oldest values erased when exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tampering with default is only way to remove old results. Default value is 5000.

rubrics_metrics.name: lines
rubrics_metrics.description: lines: if positive, gp prints at most that many lines from each result, finishing last line with [+++] if more is suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various print commands unaffected (use print(%) or \a to view full result). If screen width unknown, a line is assumed 80 characters. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: linewrap
rubrics_metrics.description: linewrap: if positive, gp wraps every single line after printing that many characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 0 (unset).

rubrics_metrics.name: log modes
rubrics_metrics.description: log: 0 (off) or 1,2,3 (on) controlling logging. When on, gp opens a log file and writes commands and results to it (appends to existing file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 = plain logfile; 2 = emit color codes to logfile (if colors set); 3 = write LaTeX output to logfile (customizable via TeXstyle). Default 0. Use logfile default to set file name.

rubrics_metrics.name: logfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: logfile: name of log file used when logging is on; environment and time expansion performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is "pari.log".

rubrics_metrics.name: nbthreads meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: nbthreads: number of threads to use for parallel computing; exact meaning depends on multithreading engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: single: always one thread; pthread: number of threads (unlimited, default = number of cores); mpi: number of MPI processes (limited by mpirun allocation, default use all allocated processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: new galois format toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: new_galois_format: if on (1), polgalois uses a different, more consistent naming scheme for Galois groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided so scripts can control behavior and avoid breaking. Default 0; will change to 1 in next major version.

rubrics_metrics.name: output modes
rubrics_metrics.description: output: 0 = raw, 1 = prettymatrix, 3 = external prettyprint. Controls how objects are printed irrespective of real number format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: raw = text equivalent to input (easy to copy/paste); prettymatrix = matrices printed as boxes (prettier but not usable as input); external prettyprint pipes LaTeX-format output to external prettyprinter (controlled by prettyprinter). Objects can be printed in any of the three formats at any time using \a, \m, and \B. Default 1 (prettymatrix).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisize guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: parisize: stack size in bytes used by gp and programs using the PARI library; PARI uses this stack for computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to increase parisize in gprc to a value appropriate for typical computations. Also set parisizemax to a larger value so PARI can grow the stack up to parisizemax when needed and then restore to parisize. Default 4M (32-bit) or 8M (64-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisizemax guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: parisizemax: maximum size the stack can grow to (in bytes). If zero, stack will not automatically grow and is limited to parisize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend setting to a non-zero value appropriate for your machine. PARI will try to fit computations within parisize bytes, but can increase up to parisizemax when needed. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: primelimit default and deprecation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: primelimit: gp precomputes primes less than primelimit at initialization and can build fast sieves to iterate primes up to primelimit^2; many arithmetic functions use this table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximal value depends on machine bitness; PARI guarantees the first 6547 primes (up to 65557) are precomputed even if primelimit is 1. This default is only used at startup; changing it later does not recompute the table. Deprecated uses: primelimit-based assumptions in some algebraic number theory functions are deprecated; also factor(N,0) (partial factor by removing primes <= primelimit) is deprecated — use factor(N,bound) instead. Default value is 500k.

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt default and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: prompt: string printed as prompt; supports escape sequences (\e, \n, \\ etc.) and is processed by strftime for time/date expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care with readline: escape sequences may cause display bugs unless braced with \[ and \]. PariEmacs needs to know prompt pattern to separate input from previous gp results; adapting automatically to arbitrary prompts is nontrivial (see PariEmacs docs). Default value is "?\n" (document shows "?\n").

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt_cont default
rubrics_metrics.description: prompt_cont: string printed as prompt for continuation lines (applies to the same caveats as prompt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is "".

rubrics_metrics.name: psfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: psfile: name of default file where gp dumps PostScript drawings (appended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment and time expansion performed. Default is "pari.ps".

rubrics_metrics.name: readline toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: readline: switches GNU readline line-editing facilities on/off for gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to disable if gp runs in environments that interact badly with readline (e.g., Sun cmdtool). When off, advanced editing like completion and history are not available. Default 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: realbitprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: realbitprecision: number of significant bits used to convert exact inputs to transcendental functions or to create absolute floating constants; also influences internal precision used for t_REAL numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most PARI functions handle precision on word basis (increments of 32/64 bits), so bit precision may be larger than expected. The value shown by default(realbitprecision) is internal bits, not printed decimal digits. Example usage and interaction with realprecision and \p are shown in docs. Default 128 (64-bit) or 96 (32-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: realprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: realprecision: number of significant decimal digits used to convert exact inputs to transcendental functions or create floating constants; also used for printing t_REAL unless overridden by format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI's internal precision works on a word basis (increments of 32/64 bits), so internal digits may exceed requested decimal digits (e.g., one word on 64-bit gives 19 decimal digits). default(realprecision) returns internal significant digits, not shown digits. Default 38 (64-bit) or 28 (32-bit).

rubrics_metrics.name: recover toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: recover: 1 (on) or 0 (off). If set to 0, any error becomes fatal and gp exits immediately. Useful in batch scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: secure toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: secure: 1 (on) or 0 (off). If on, the system and extern commands are disabled to prevent executing arbitrary UNIX commands from gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gp will ask for confirmation before allowing you (or a script) to unset this toggle. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: seriesprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: seriesprecision: number of significant terms when converting polynomials or rational functions to power series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: simplify: 1 (on) or 0 (off). When on, PARI library automatically simplifies certain types (e.g., rational to integer, rational functions to polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only some automatic simplifications are done; when disabled use simplify function explicitly to reduce objects to simplest types recursively (see \y). Default 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: sopath default
rubrics_metrics.description: sopath: list of directories searched when installing an external symbol from a shared library if the library name is not absolute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format is colon-separated (or semicolon on DOS/Windows). Environment expansion performed. Default is "" (empty list) meaning install looks in current directory if name is not absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictargs toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: strictargs: if on (1), all arguments to user functions are mandatory unless the function supplies an explicit default; otherwise missing arguments default to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to functions defined while strictargs is on; changing strictargs does not affect previously defined functions. Example fun(a,b=2)=a+b: with strictargs on, fun() triggers missing mandatory argument 'a'. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictmatch (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: strictmatch: obsolete toggle, now a no-op.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented as obsolete; no behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: threadsize
rubrics_metrics.description: threadsize: in parallel mode, size in bytes of the private stack for each thread; total memory allocated is parisize + nbthreads × threadsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If set to 0, value used is same as parisize. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: threadsizemax
rubrics_metrics.description: threadsizemax: maximal size in bytes of stacks of each thread in parallel mode, so total memory allocated will be between parisize + nbthreads × threadsize and parisize + nbthreads × threadsizemax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If set to 0, value used is same as threadsize. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: timer toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: timer: 1 (on) or 0 (off). When on, each instruction sequence is timed and printed immediately before output as user CPU time (not including printing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing printed as e.g. 'time = 108 ms.' Nothing printed if time negligible (<1ms). Timings not shown when defining user functions or aliases, or installing a symbol. Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required tools for compiling PARI
rubrics_metrics.description: Compiling PARI requires an ANSI C or C++ compiler (gcc/g++ recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Mac OS X this is in Xcode or Command-line tools. The PARI kernel benefits from gcc optimizations. Optional but useful libraries/programs: GNU MP (gmp), GNU readline, GNU emacs + PariEmacs, gzip/gunzip/gzcat, perl (provides extended online help). See download page for pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure basic usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Run ./Configure in top-level directory to configure PARI/GP build; use --prefix to change installation prefix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure creates build directory Oosname-arch. Inspect messages prefixed by ### for problems, and config.log in build directory for debugging. Use ./Configure --prefix=/an/exotic/directory to change install prefix. For interactive Configure use ./Configure -a.

rubrics_metrics.name: --tune and advanced Configure flags
rubrics_metrics.description: --tune fine tunes library for host by running many comparative tests and creates tune.h; other flags include --graphic=lib, --time=function, --with-runtime-perl=perl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: --tune can take ~30 minutes and gives a small performance boost; if using GMP, tune it first. --graphic selects graphics backend (X11, Qt, fltk, ps, win32). --time chooses timing function (getrusage, clock_gettime, times, ftime). --with-runtime-perl picks runtime perl for gphelp/tex2mail (useful for cross-compiling).

rubrics_metrics.name: --mt engine and --enable-tls
rubrics_metrics.description: --mt=engine selects multithreading engine: single, pthread, mpi. --enable-tls builds thread-safe version of library (implied by --mt=pthread).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: single: default no parallelism. pthread: POSIX threads (multi-core); implies --enable-tls and requires pthread library. mpi: use MPI interface (requires MPI library and usually set CC=mpicc). --enable-tls slows libpari.so by ~15%; consider static libpari.a for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation targets and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: To compile run 'make all' (build gp and docs) or 'make gp' (build gp only). To test, run 'make bench' or 'make dobench'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If make supports parallel jobs, build in Oosname-arch directory with make -jN. make bench runs quick verification tests and may build multiple gp variants (gp-sta, gp-dyn) and run tests on both. If BUG messages show up, inspect difference files and consider reporting bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure -a interactive mode and troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: If Configure fails use './Configure -a' for interactive mode to answer detailed questions; default answers may still fail. Inspect messages and consider bug report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use config.log for diagnostics. If optional libraries (gmp, readline, X11, perl, gunzip) not found, Configure may fail — follow section 3 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment variables affecting Configure/linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure lets CC, DLLD, LD override defaults. CFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, LDFLAGS are appended; C_INCLUDE_PATH and LIBRARY_PATH are prepended to include/library search lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., env CC=cc Configure. To disable inlining add -DDISABLE_INLINE to CFLAGS; disable volatile keyword with -DDISABLE_VOLATILE. For readline issues set --with-readline or --with-readline-lib/--with-readline-include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging/profiling build modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure -g creates a debug-suitable build directory; Configure -pg creates a profiling build for gprof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimized gp built by default. Use .dbg or .prf directories to build special-purpose binaries (make gp in those directories or invoke make gp.dbg / make gp.prf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiprecision kernel selection
rubrics_metrics.description: --kernel=Level0-Level1 selects multiprecision kernel levels: Level0 (auto/none/architectural micro-kernels) and Level1 (auto/none/gmp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully qualified kernel name is Level0-Level1. Aliases without dash mean name-none; 'gmp' stands for auto-gmp. Default auto-auto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readline known problems and Configure options
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure does not always find readline; use --with-readline[=prefix], --with-readline-lib, or --with-readline-include to point to installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Linux you need both readline and readline-devel (and sometimes ncurses-devel). On OS X, the system-supplied fake readline is insufficient; consult PARI FAQ for step-by-step solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: make bench known-problem handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'BUG' shows up in make bench, diagnostic messages point to differences between expected and actual output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect difference files to decide if it's a PARI bug; use make dobench to test only default binary. For cross-compiling set RUNTEST environment variable to a program that can run target binaries (e.g., emulator).
